pico.population: Adult patients (>=18 years) with confirmed or suspected splenic lesions or haematological malignancies (including lymphoma, leukaemia, and metastatic disease involving the spleen) undergoing contrast-enhanced CT, MRI, or PET-CT imaging in oncology or radiology departments.
pico.intervention: Radiomics feature extraction from splenic medical images — including first-order statistical features (intensity histogram, entropy, kurtosis), texture features (GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, GLDM), shape and morphological descriptors, and wavelet-transformed features — combined with machine learning or deep learning classifiers (e.g., SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, CNN) to detect, characterise, and classify cancerous splenic involvement.
pico.comparison: Conventional radiological assessment by radiologists using visual inspection and qualitative criteria, standard clinical biomarkers (LDH, beta-2 microglobulin, CBC), histopathological biopsy as the gold standard, and single-feature or non-radiomic imaging approaches.
pico.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of radiomics models for detecting malignant splenic lesions — measured by AUC-ROC, sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive value; ability to differentiate benign vs. malignant splenic pathology; feature importance rankings identifying the most discriminative radiomic signatures; and model generalisation across imaging protocols and patient cohorts.
pico.hypothesis: Radiomics features extracted from routine CT or MRI images of the spleen can accurately detect and classify cancerous splenic involvement — including primary splenic malignancies and secondary metastatic disease — with diagnostic performance comparable to or exceeding conventional radiological assessment, thereby offering a non-invasive, reproducible biomarker for splenic cancer detection.

key_findings: CT-based radiomics achieves 97% diagnostic accuracy for lymphoma vs benign splenomegaly differentiation using LASSO-selected features [R1]
Radiomic features from spleen CT can differentiate lymphoma subtypes (HL, DLBCL, MCL, FL) using Random Forest classifiers [R2]
ComBat harmonization significantly improves radiomic feature stability across multi-center CT protocols when using spleen as internal reference [R3]
Multi-phase CT protocols (non-contrast, arterial, portal venous) provide optimal feature extraction for splenic radiomics [R4]
First-order statistics and texture features (GLCM, GLRLM) show highest discriminative power for malignant splenic pathology [R1, R2]
consensus_points: Portal venous phase CT provides optimal texture feature extraction for splenic parenchyma analysis across studies
Random Forest classifiers consistently outperform other ML algorithms for limited sample sizes in splenic radiomics
LASSO regression effectively selects discriminative features while controlling for overfitting
Texture features derived from wavelet transforms demonstrate superior discriminative power
contested_areas: Optimal imaging modality: limited evidence comparing CT vs MRI vs PET-CT for splenic radiomics
Segmentation methodology: manual vs semi-automated vs fully automated approaches lack comparative performance data
Multi-center harmonization: ComBat vs alternative methods require systematic comparison
research_gaps: Direct comparison studies between radiomics and radiologist performance for splenic lymphoma detection
Multi-center prospective validation cohorts with standardized imaging protocols
Integration of radiomics with clinical biomarkers (LDH, β2-microglobulin) for comprehensive diagnostic models
Large-scale studies assessing generalizability across diverse lymphoma subtypes and ethnic populations
Regulatory pathway definition for spleen radiomics software as medical device
recommended_methods: Portal venous phase CT with ≤3mm slice thickness based on [R1, R2, R4]
ComBat harmonization for multi-center datasets based on [R3]
Semi-automated segmentation with ICC >0.85 for reproducibility
LASSO feature selection followed by Random Forest classification based on [R1, R2]
External validation cohort inclusion with at least 50% of training cohort size
benchmark_datasets: Medical Segmentation Decathlon: spleen segmentation datasets
Currently no dedicated splenic lymphoma radiomics benchmark datasets
key_metrics: AUC-ROC — observed range: 0.89–0.97 across studies [R1, R2]
ICC for feature reproducibility — minimum threshold: >0.80
imaging_protocols: CT: portal venous phase, slice thickness ≤3mm — supported by [R1, R2, R4]
Contrast: standard iodine-based contrast media at 120-140 mL
MRI: limited evidence, T2-weighted and DWI sequences suggested

agent_hints.population_planner: Focus on adult lymphoma patients with contrast-enhanced CT imaging. Include lymphoma subtypes (HL, DLBCL, MCL, FL) as per [R2]. Target cohort size 150-300 patients based on [R1, R2], with histopathological confirmation. Exclude patients with prior splenic interventions.
agent_hints.segmentation_agent: Use semi-automated spleen segmentation with expert radiologist oversight. Employ U-Net architecture as in [R6], but require ICC >0.85 for reproducibility. Segment entire spleen parenchyma including focal lesions. Use portal venous phase CT images with ≤3mm slice thickness.
agent_hints.feature_extraction: Extract IBSI-compliant features using PyRadiomics. Focus on texture features (GLCM, GLRLM) and shape descriptors as discriminative power shown in [R1, R2]. Include wavelet transforms. Apply ComBat harmonization for inter-scanner variability as per [R3]. Resample to 1×1×1 mm voxels.
agent_hints.modeling_agent: Implement Random Forest classifier with 500 trees based on superior performance in [R1, R2]. Use LASSO for feature selection. Apply 10-fold cross-validation. Address class imbalance with SMOTE. Train on ≥100 patients as per literature evidence.
agent_hints.validation_agent: Include external validation cohort from different institution. Report AUC-ROC, sensitivity, specificity, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. Compare performance against conventional radiologist assessment. Use DeLong test for AUC comparison. Adhere to TRIPOD reporting guidelines.
agent_hints.reporter_agent: Highlight 97% diagnostic accuracy benchmark from [R1], lymphoma subtype differentiation capability from [R2], and multi-center harmonization importance from [R3]. Discuss clinical translation pathway and regulatory considerations. Address limitations in generalizability and need for prospective validation.
